parole.significato: Synonym of money.
parole.testo: Probably from Egyptian Arabic قرش (ʔerš, “piastre, Ottoman penny”). See also smackers, smackeroo, smackeroonies.

parole.testo: From Egyptian Arabic بهار (bahār) or other dialects, Arabic بُهَار (buhār).

parole.significato: An Arab dish of eggs cooked in a pancake, bound to a meat or vegetable filling.
parole.testo: From Egyptian Arabic عِجّة (ʕegga), from Arabic عُجَّة (ʕujja), from ع ج ج (ʕ j j) meaning "to be overcrowded or jammed pack", as the meal is typically packed or stuffed with chop-meat and/or various vegetable fillings.

parole.significato: A clumsy or uncouth person.
parole.testo: From Quranic Arabic جالُوت (jālūt, pronounced galūt in Egyptian Arabic), proper name equivalent to English Goliath, giant warrior of the ancient Philistine ethnicity; cf. connotations of derogatory uses of English Philistine. Doublet of goliath.

parole.significato: An Egyptian dancing girl
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic غازية (ḡāziyya), plural غوازي (ḡawāzi).

parole.significato: go away
parole.testo: Most likely borrowed from Egyptian Arabic إِمْشِي (ʔimši, “go away!”, literally “walk!”), itself ultimately from older Arabic اِمْشِ (imši, id). For the derivation from Egyptian Arabic, compare shufti.

parole.testo: From Egyptian Arabic خَمْسِين (ḵamsīn, “fifty”); see khamaseen for more.

parole.significato: An Egyptian dish of rice, macaroni and lentils topped with a tomato-vinegar sauce and garnishes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic كُشَرِي (košarī).

parole.significato: The spongy fibers of the fruit of a cucurbitaceous plant (Luffa aegyptiaca).
parole.testo: From Egyptian Arabic لُوف (lūf).

parole.significato: There is no more; I have nothing.
parole.testo: From Egyptian Arabic مفيش (mafīš), eventually from ما (ma, mā, “not”) + في (fī, “there is”) + ـش (-š, negation ending). Borrowed into English by travelers and the British military.

parole.significato: mad; crazy
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic مجنون (magnūn).

parole.significato: A rejected name for radium.
parole.testo: *From Masr + -ium, ultimately derived from Egyptian Arabic مصر.

parole.significato: The ichneumon, or Egyptian mongoose.
parole.testo: From Egyptian Arabic نمس (nims).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic أم علي (ʔumm ʕali, literally “Ali's mother”).

parole.significato: A village head man in Egypt.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic عمدة (ʕumda), from Arabic عُمْدَة (ʕumda).

parole.significato: One of the main types of cheese in Egypt, made from cows' milk or from buffalo milk.
parole.testo: Calque of Egyptian Arabic جبنة رومي (gibna rumī).

parole.significato: A device used since ancient times in the Middle East to raise water from a well or other low point, consisting of a piv…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic شادوف (šadūf); see further at that entry.

parole.significato: An Arabic water-pipe, or hookah.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic شيشة (šīša), from Ottoman Turkish شیشه şişe, from Classical Persian شیشه (šīša, “glass, mirror”).

parole.significato: A brief glance.
parole.testo: UK 1940s, originally military slang. From Egyptian Arabic شُفْتِ، شُفْتِي (šufti, “have you seen?”, literally “you saw”), a conjugation of شَاف (šāf, “to see”).

parole.significato: An old Egyptian unit of dry measure.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian Arabic.

parole.significato: One of a minority religious community of Coptic Christians who work as Cairo's informal garbage collectors.
parole.testo: Egyptian Arabic زبالين
